introduce:
Lie down on your back, and put your hands beneath your hips for support. 

Then lift your legs up until they form a right angle with the floor. 

Slowly bring your legs back down and repeat the exercise.
name: LEG RAISES

tips.text: This workout should be done on a mat.
Raise up your legs faster and put them down slower.
Your back should always be flat on the floor.
Keep your legs as straight as possible.
Don't pull your shoulders up off the floor.
Exhale when lifting your legs, and inhale when lowering them.
If you feel it's too hard, put a little bend in your knees.
You shouldn't feel any pressure in your chest and shoulder area.
This exercise targets your lower abdominals.

introduce: Start on all fours with your knees under butt and your hands under shoulders. \n\nThen lift your right leg and squeeze your butt as much as you can. Go back to the start position and repeat the exercise.
name: DONKEY KICKS RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this workout on a mat.
Keep your lifted leg at a 90 degree angle.
To get better results, keep your core tight.
Don't lift your knee higher than your back.
Exhale when lifting your leg, and inhale when lowering it.
This exercise tones your gluteus, and can also work on your hamstrings.

introduce: Lie on your back with knees bent and feet flat on the floor. Put your arms flat at your sides. \n\nThen lift your butt up and down.
name: BUTT BRIDGE

tips.text: This workout should be done on a mat.
Keep your feet around shoulder width apart.
Exhale when lifting your butt, and inhale when lowering it.
This exercise really works on your glutes.
This exercise strengthens your lower back.

introduce: Start on all fours with your knees under your butt and your hands under your shoulders. \n\nThen lift your left leg and squeeze your butt as much as you can. Go back to the start position and repeat the exercise.
name: DONKEY KICKS LEFT

tips.text: Please do this workout on a mat.
Keep your lifted leg at a 90 degree angle.
To get better results, keep your core tight.
Don't lift your knee higher than your back.
Exhale when lifting your leg, and inhale when lowering it.
This exercise tones your gluteus, and can also work on your hamstrings.

introduce:
Start in the straight arm plank position.

Lift your right hand to tap your left shoulder. 

Return to the start position and repeat with the other hand.
name: PLANK TAPS

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Keep your head, spine and neck in line.
Exhale when tapping your shoulders, and inhale when putting your hands down.
This exercise works on your core and upper body, and also engages your shoulders.
This exercise can relieve your lower back pain.

introduce:
Lie on your back with your knees up at a 90 degree angle and your arms lifted towards the ceiling. 

Lower your right leg, and extend your left arm above your head. 

Hold it for one second, then return to the start position and repeat with the other side.
name: DEAD BUG

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please always keep your lower back pressed against the floor.
Please don\'t arch your back.
Too hard? Just extend your arms or legs.
This exercise can help relieve lower back pain.
Inhale when lifting your arm and opposite leg, and exhale when lowering them.

introduce: Lie on your left side with your head resting on your left arm and knees bent. \n\nLift your right knee upwards while keeping your heels touching, then go back to the starting position. Repeat the exercise.
name: PILATES CLAMSHELL RIGHT

tips.text: Please do it on a mat.
Please keep your pelvis and torso stable during the exercise.
Please bring your bottom waist away from the floor.
Exhale as you lift the top knee up, and inhale as you lower it.
This exercise strengthens your glutes and thighs.

introduce: Lie on your right side with your head resting on your right arm and knees bent. \n\nLift your left knee upwards while keeping your heels touching, then go back to the starting position. Repeat the exercise.
name: PILATES CLAMSHELL LEFT

tips.text: Please do it on a mat.
Please keep your pelvis and torso stable during the exercise.
Please bring your bottom waist away from the floor.
Exhale as you lift the top knee up, and inhale as you lower it.
This exercise strengthens your glutes and thighs.

introduce: Lie on your back with your legs extended and your hands underneath your hips.\n\nSlightly lift your legs and shoulders, and then alternately cross your legs over one another.
name: CRISSCROSS

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your abs tight.
Please keep your feet off the ground.
Don’t forget to breathe.
Try to keep your legs as straight as you can.
It’s a good exercise for your abs and thighs.

introduce: Lie on your back with your knees bent, feet flat on the ground and hands underneath your hips. \n\nRaise your legs to the tabletop position; drop your left foot towards the ground. Tap the ground with your toes; then raise the leg back. Switch sides, and repeat the exercise.
name: TOE TAP

tips.text: Please prepare a mat.
Keep your knee steady as you drop your leg towards the ground.
Exhale as you drop your leg; inhale as you bring it back.

introduce: Lie on your stomach with your forearms on the floor and your elbows under your shoulders. Extend your legs with the tops of your feet on the floor. \n\nInhale, lift your upper body and extend your neck away from your shoulders. Hold this position.
name: SPHINX POSE

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Draw your shoulders away from your ears.
This exercise stretches your chest, shoulders, and abdomen.
This exercise strengthens your spine and helps ease your lower back pain.
Breathe regularly.

introduce:
Lie flat on a mat, extend your legs at an angle from the mat. Engage your core, lift your shoulders off the mat with arms straight by your ears, shoulder-width apart. Inhale to prepare.

Exhale, bend your knees towards your chest as you sweep your arms out to the sides, reaching around to grasp your shins or ankles and squeeze.

Inhale, reach your arms over your head and keep your legs long.

Repeat the exercise.
name: DOUBLE LEG STRETCH

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep your shoulders lifted.
Please keep your core engaged.
This exercise can stabilize your core muscles.
This exercise helps with your abdominal strength.

introduce:
Lie flat on your back, and bend your knees into the chest. Place your hands behind your head to support your head with your fingertips.

Lift your head, neck, and shoulders off the mat, engaging your abdominal muscles.

Extend your right leg out straight into the air while simultaneously rotating your upper body to bring your right elbow towards your left bent knee. 

Switch your legs as you bring your left elbow toward your right knee. 

Repeat the exercise.
name: PILATES CRISS CROSS

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please do not strain your neck and head.
Please keep your core tight.
Please do not hold your breath.
Please keep the elbows wide.
Please make sure your pelvis is stable.
This exercise helps you build strong obliques and a more defined waistline.

introduce:
Lie flat on a mat, extend your leg straight toward the ceiling.

Inhale, circle your left leg towards your right thigh, straight down but cannot be flat against the mat. 

Exhale and lift up to the start position.

Repeat and reverse the exercise in the opposite direction.
name: SINGLE LEG CIRCLES LEFT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep the toes of your left leg pointed.
Please keep your move within the frame of your body.
This exercise works on the stability of your pelvis.

introduce:
Lie flat on a mat, draw your right knee in towards the chest and then extend your leg straight toward the ceiling.

Inhale, circle your right leg towards your left thigh, straight down but cannot be flat against the mat. 

Exhale and lift up to the start position.

Repeat and reverse the exercise in the opposite direction.
name: SINGLE LEG CIRCLES RIGHT

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please keep the toes of your right leg pointed.
Please keep your move within the frame of your body.
This exercise works on the stability of your pelvis.

introduce:
Lie flat on your back with your legs extended and your arms reaching overhead. Keep your legs together and your toes pointed. Inhale to prepare. 

Exhale, begin to slowly peel your spine off the mat, one vertebra at a time until your body is in a seated position, with your arms reaching towards your toes.

Inhale at the top, and as you exhale, slowly begin to roll back down.

Repeat the exercise.
name: ROLL UP

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please initiate the movement from your core, instead of your arms.
This exercise can strengthen abdominal muscles.

introduce:
Sit on a mat with your legs extended. Flex your feet and keep your legs together. Extend your arms to the sides, parallel to the floor. Inhale deeply to prepare.

Exhale, twist your body towards one side, double pulse.

Inhale as you return to the center. Exhale, twist towards the opposite direction and double pulse.

Repeat the exercise.
name: SPINE TWIST

tips.text: Please do this on a mat.
Please do not move your pelvis.
Please keep your legs extended.
Please make sure your upper body moves in one piece.
This exercise promotes good posture.
